question: When solid lead(II) nitrate is heated, a yellow residue ( PbO ) is left behind and two gases are evolved — one is reddish-brown and the other supports combustion. Which gases are evolved?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitrogen dioxide and oxygen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When **solid lead(II) nitrate (Pb(NO₃)₂)** is heated, it undergoes **thermal decomposition**, breaking down into **lead(II) oxide (PbO)**, **nitrogen dioxide (NO₂)**, and **oxygen (O₂)**.
 
• The **yellow residue** left behind after heating is **lead(II) oxide (PbO)**. This confirms the decomposition of lead(II) nitrate.
 
• The reddish-brown gas evolved is **nitrogen dioxide (NO₂)**, which is a characteristic product of the decomposition of nitrates containing heavy metals.
 
• The gas that supports combustion is **oxygen (O₂)**, which is also released during the decomposition process.
 
• The reaction can be represented as: Pb(NO₃)₂ (s) → PbO (s) + 2NO₂ (g) + ½ O₂ (g)
